studies.label: Two-session laboratory experiment: analytical essays with randomized AI access, then unaided writing approximately one week later
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Students were individually randomized to computers within a chosen time slot; the two parallel labs were then randomly assigned to opposite conditions. The cluster counts describe lab-by-time-slot delivery groups, one per arm in each of the eight slots, rather than distinct buildings (PDF p. 6, Section 2.1; PDF p. 54, Figure A3 notes). The paper uses student-level heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors and time-slot fixed effects; it does not report clustering by lab/time slot or an adjustment for similarity scores sharing essays (PDF p. 12, Section 3.3; PDF p. 41, Table 5 notes).

arms.name: AI-allowed
arms.description: Any generative AI tool permitted during Session One learning and essay writing; a dedicated ChatGPT (GPT-4o) account was supplied. Standard online resources were also permitted. AI and other external resources were prohibited for all knowledge tests and for the Session Two essay (PDF pp. 7-10, Sections 2.1-2.2; PDF p. 53, Figure A2). Arm counts refer to assigned sign-ups and the Session One study sample, not the outcome-specific essay sample.

arms.name: AI-forbidden
arms.description: Generative AI prohibited during Session One learning and essay writing; standard online resources such as Google, Wikipedia, and the college library website were permitted. AI and other external resources were prohibited for all knowledge tests and for the Session Two essay (PDF pp. 7-10, Sections 2.1-2.2; PDF p. 53, Figure A2). Arm counts refer to assigned sign-ups and the Session One study sample, not the outcome-specific essay sample.

studies.task: Middlebury College undergraduates read about randomly assigned blockchain technology, carbon capture, or CRISPR gene editing and write an analytical essay, then write to a complementary prompt on the same topic without AI or other resources in the later session (PDF pp. 7-10, Sections 2.1-3.1).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (GPT-4o); any generative AI tool was permitted
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 2.1, Treatment; the model release year is not printed

preregistration.where: AEA RCT Registry, AEARCTR-0015806, https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/trials/15806 (linked on PDF p. 1); pre-analysis plan explicitly discussed on PDF p. 13, Section 3.4. The external registration and plan were not retrieved.
preregistration.primary_outcome: Overall essay quality rating and the average quality index are explicitly identified as the primary essay-based outcomes in the pre-analysis plan (PDF p. 13, Section 3.4). The paper does not identify within-group similarity as a preregistered primary outcome.

estimates.outcome: Within-group similarity, Session One essays (AI available)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: A sentence-embedding model fine-tuned from MPNet, with no exact checkpoint stated. For each student's essay, the outcome is its average pairwise cosine similarity with all other essays in the same assigned treatment × topic × prompt cell. The regression has one similarity score per student, with one essay per session; higher values mean greater between-student similarity (PDF p. 14, Section 3.4; PDF p. 41, Table 5, Panel B notes).

stats.difference_is: AI-allowed minus AI-forbidden; the adjusted assignment coefficient is recorded under regression

regression.model: OLS intent-to-treat coefficient on assignment to AI-allowed, with Session One time-slot fixed effects and controls selected through double-lasso; outcome is raw average cosine similarity (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 3.3; PDF p. 41, Table 5 notes).

estimates.notes: Raw similarity sign is retained. The estimate is the randomized-access ITT contrast; the accompanying instrumental-variable TOT is not a separate arm contrast. Both arms could use standard online resources during Session One, supporting ai_vs_bau. The treatment-arm mean is not printed and is not reconstructed from the adjusted coefficient. The outcome-specific treatment count is not printed separately and is not obtained by subtracting the control count from the total. Figures 6 and A7 show standardized estimates and confidence intervals only graphically; no values were digitized (PDF p. 34; PDF p. 58). The paper reports student-level robust uncertainty without a stated adjustment for dependence between similarity scores that share essays. The outcome was produced with AI available to the treatment arm.

open_items: Neither treatment-arm mean, arm-level standard deviation, nor arm-mean standard error for within-group similarity is printed. No treatment mean was computed from an adjusted coefficient (PDF p. 41, Table 5, Panel B).

The outcome-specific treated participant count is not separately printed for either similarity analysis. Only the printed control and total counts are entered; treatment counts are null under the no-computation rule (PDF p. 41, Table 5, Panel B).

Numerical confidence limits, exact p-values, and numerical standardized similarity effects are not printed for these contrasts. Figures 6 and A7 show standardized effects and intervals graphically (PDF pp. 34 and 58).
The exact sentence-embedding checkpoint is not stated; only a sentence-embedding model fine-tuned from MPNet is identified (PDF p. 41, Table 5 notes).
The release year of GPT-4o is not printed in the paper; ai_tool.year is null (PDF p. 8, Treatment).

No adjustment is described for lab/time-slot delivery groups or for dependence between participant similarity scores sharing essays. se_basis records the paper’s participant-level robust analysis, not an independently verified dependence correction (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 3.3; PDF p. 41, Table 5 notes).

The paper does not provide a complete account of outcome-specific missing essays. The grading rule for empty or very short essays applies to AI grading and cannot establish the similarity-analysis exclusions (PDF p. 37, Table 1; PDF p. 41, Table 5; PDF p. 75, Appendix B.4).

The paper names preregistered primary essay-quality outcomes but does not establish preregistered-primary status for either similarity outcome; the linked registry and pre-analysis plan were not independently read (PDF p. 1; PDF p. 13, Section 3.4).
notes: Extraction is restricted to the two within-group essay-similarity outcomes under Review 1. The is_own_paper flag follows the codebook's explicit decision. All numerical results come from the requested September PDF; the screening form supplies the study/arm names and outcome IDs. An in-memory Markdown conversion of the September PDF was read consecutively from start to end, including all appendices, and every cited page was checked with PyMuPDF text extraction. The study-level analyzed count describes Session One attendees; the estimates use the separate essay-analysis counts printed in Table 5. Table A4 agrees with Table 5 on the essay-text analysis totals in this version (PDF p. 66). Individual assignment follows the documented random allocation of students to computers; the additional lab-by-slot assignment and the paper's unclustered uncertainty are disclosed separately. The task is coded other, consistent with the screening form's analytical-essay task; eligibility is through between-writer similarity. No shared-participant claim with another paper is stated, consistent with sample_overlap in the reconciled form; shared_sample is null. No standardized effects, sample-size differences, confidence limits, or other derived statistics were computed. Repeated-session outcomes are not a randomized within-person crossover.
